candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS Merko Ehitus reported a weaker top-line and operating performance in 2025 as several large construction projects completed and new contract signing was slower during 2024 and the first half of 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue declined 42.3% to EUR 310.9 million from EUR 539.0 million, while gross profit fell to EUR 55.9 million from EUR 95.9 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Despite the lower volume, gross margin improved slightly to 18.0% from 17.8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Operating profit decreased 52.6% to EUR 34.3 million, and the operating margin narrowed to 11.0% from 13.4%, reflecting the completion of highly profitable contracts and a return to more typical sector margins amid strong competition.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: EBITDA fell to EUR 37.5 million from EUR 75.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Profit before tax declined to EUR 44.8 million from EUR 76.4 million, while net profit attributable to shareholders decreased to EUR 39.9 million from EUR 64.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: However, the net margin improved to 12.8% from 12.0%, supported partly by lower finance costs and a EUR 10.4 million contribution from joint ventures.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Earnings per share fell to EUR 2.26 from EUR 3.65.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Construction services remained the main business, but revenue fell 49.9% to EUR 237.6 million and operating profit declined 56.8% to EUR 25.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Real estate development revenue increased 13.8% to EUR 73.4 million, supported by the sale of 358 apartments compared with 323 in 2024, although segment operating profit fell 18.8% to EUR 13.4 million as margins declined and a property in Norway was written down.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The group also started more than three times as many new apartments as in the prior year.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Market conditions remained uncertain, with weak private investment, subdued construction activity in Estonia and reduced renewable-energy investment, although defence and infrastructure spending supported demand.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: New construction contracts worth EUR 362.8 million were signed, lifting the secured order book 37.1% to EUR 466.9 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Major contracts included Rail Baltica, defence-related projects, a Pärnu hotel and conference centre, and wind-farm infrastructure.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The largest contracts in Merko’s history for two phases of the Rūdninkai defence campus were signed early in 2026 and are expected to contribute from 2026 onward.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Cash flow weakened materially: operating cash flow was negative at EUR 1.7 million compared with positive cash flow of EUR 57.8 million in 2024, mainly because of higher inventories and construction-related working-capital movements.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Cash and cash equivalents declined to EUR 41.4 million from EUR 91.9 million after EUR 33.6 million of dividends were paid.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Nevertheless, equity increased to EUR 260.6 million, the equity ratio strengthened to 62.8% from 56.9%, and interest-bearing liabilities remained moderate at 8.0% of assets.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Management proposed a EUR 1.25-per-share dividend, totaling EUR 22.1 million, equivalent to a 55% payout ratio.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K6, K7, and K8 are all PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. K4 (PPP business expansion) and K5 (Connecto network companies investment) are MISSING - no mention of real estate development agreements in Krulli/Uus-Karlowa or Connecto brand contributions. While most HIGH importance criteria are covered, the absence of two HIGH items prevents a 'Yes' rating, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
